title: M31.10 security hardening: email verification — required identity, non-mutating GET, atomic consume, trusted-origin links
head: feat/m31-10-security-hardening
body:
## M31.10 — email-verification security hardening (owner directive)

**Follow-up to PR #5** — PR #5 (M31) was MERGED by the owner at 2026-11-24T02:01Z (`77bd87c`), and merged PRs are immutable, so this hardening lands as a new reviewable PR on top of the exact merged state (`6dee86b`, tree-identical to `origin/main`). **Left unmerged for owner review — never self-merged.**

### Baseline
- Branch base: `6dee86b` (PR #5 head; `git diff 6dee86b origin/main` = empty)
- Endpoint commit: `be38926`

### The four requirements, implemented and regression-tested

1. **Registration REQUIRES an identity** — closes the email-verification bypass. `POST /api/auth/register` previously accepted an identity-less body, which skipped the verification lifecycle entirely (no token, trust gates never applied). Every new registration is now identity-aware: PRIVATE profile + verification token issued unconditionally. **Legacy accounts and existing user records are preserved exactly** — no backfill, no reclassification (tests assert the 400, zero rows created, and an untouched pre-M31 legacy row). Google OAuth intentionally unchanged (provider-verified emails; `tests/google-oauth.test.ts` 26/26 green).
2. **GET on the confirm route is COMPLETELY NON-MUTATING** — automated link scanners / prefetchers (SafeLinks, unfurlers) can no longer consume single-use tokens. GET = read-only state inspection + 302 into the new public `#/verify-email` page carrying the token; ONLY the explicit user confirmation (POST from that page) consumes it. Scanner-simulation regression: 3 GETs leave the token unconsumed and the user unverified; the subsequent POST verifies.
3. **Atomic consumption** — token consume (`consumedAt`) and `emailVerifiedAt` update run in ONE Prisma interactive transaction (bounded `maxWait`/`timeout`). Regression: expired tokens leave both writes untouched; 3 concurrent confirmations verify exactly once.
4. **Absolute URLs from the trusted configured origin** — links generated ONLY via `resolveShareOrigin()` (validated `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`/`VERCEL_URL`); request headers never influence the link (structural: the builder takes only the token). Unconfigured origin → honest path-only fallback + `linkAbsolute`/`originConfigured` delivery-audit markers; the GET compat redirect falls back to the request's own origin (same-host, never a foreign host). The email link now targets the confirmation page (explicit click) instead of the consuming GET.

### New surface
- `src/views/VerifyEmailView.tsx` — public, sessionless, non-mutating confirmation page; token stripped from the address bar after read; wired into `SiteShell` + `PUBLIC_ROOT_SEGMENTS` (public so an un-onboarded new account is never bounced into a setup flow).

### Verification evidence (isolated QA DB via `scripts/ops/qa-db-env.sh` guard)

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| New regression suite `tests/m31-10-security-hardening.test.ts` | **15/15 pass** |
| Full per-file QA suite (111 files, per-file processes) | **1633 pass** — single timing flake `queue-reliability` (6 fail once during the run; **9/9 green across 4 isolated re-runs**; pre-existing timing sensitivity, not an M31.10 path) |
| Password login / Google OAuth / recovery / onboarding intact | `auth` 9/9 · `auth-routes` 11/11 · `recovery` 9/9 · `google-oauth` 26/26 · `trust-identity-registration` 15/15 · `trust-email-verification` 14/14 |
| TypeScript (`bunx tsc --noEmit`) | 0 errors |
| ESLint | 0 errors / 14 warnings (exact M31.8 baseline) |
| Schema parity | 104 models identical sqlite ↔ postgres |
| `prisma validate` both schemas | green (postgres validated with a postgres-protocol URL — the SQLite QA env var triggers its protocol guard, validation only) |
| Production standalone build | **exit 0** (2560MB heap cap; artifact 330M, BUILD_ID `GC0LBkQNWi5dA1duMlpzt`) |
| Secret scan + runtime-data scan on staged diff | clean |

### Honest scope notes
- The identity requirement is a **deliberate API contract change**: identity-less registration now returns 400. All QA fixtures/scripts were migrated to the new contract in this PR.
- Google-created accounts continue with `primaryIdentity = null` (legacy onboarding flow). Their emails are provider-verified by the OAuth flow itself. Adding identity selection to OAuth onboarding is an owner decision — recorded in the plan doc's M31.10 design notes.
- No production DDL/migration, no deployment, no email-provider setup, no security-default changes beyond the scoped hardening. No schema changes at all (104-model parity unchanged).

*Design decisions recorded in `docs/product/TRUST_ONBOARDING_AND_RIISHE_MULTI_AGENT_PLAN.md` (M31.10 section).*
